facts.fact_text: On 1 May 1999, a group of people, including the applicants, gathered in the building of the Health Workers' Trade Union.
On 1 May 1999, the group that had gathered in the building of the Health Workers' Trade Union started to walk towards the Adıyaman Amphitheatre for the May Day celebrations.
The group stated that they had obtained prior authorisation from the Adıyaman Governor and attempted to continue their march towards the Adıyaman Amphitheatre.

In his decision of 1 June 1999, the Adıyaman Public Prosecutor stated that the demonstrators had been stopped by the police, although they had been walking silently along the pavement, without presenting a danger to the public or engaging in any violent activities.
The group walking towards the Adıyaman Amphitheatre was stopped by police officers.
The police intervened to disperse the group that was attempting to continue its march towards the Adıyaman Amphitheatre.
The applicants were allegedly injured during the police intervention to disperse the group as a result of the force used by the police.
According to the incident report, thirty-eight people, including the applicants, were arrested during the incident on 1 May 1999.
Following their examination at the Adıyaman State Hospital, the applicants were taken into custody.

In his decision of 1 June 1999, the Adıyaman Public Prosecutor indicated that, pursuant to section 24 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911), the police were under an obligation to warn the group out loud to disperse.
On 30 April 1999, the Adıyaman Governor authorised the holding of May Day celebrations in the Adıyaman Amphitheatre, located in the Hasancık District.
The group stated that they had obtained prior authorisation from the Adıyaman Governor and attempted to continue their march towards the Adıyaman Amphitheatre.

In his decision of 1 June 1999, the Adıyaman Public Prosecutor stated that the demonstrators had been stopped by the police, although they had been walking silently along the pavement, without presenting a danger to the public or engaging in any violent activities.

In his decision of 1 June 1999, the Adıyaman Public Prosecutor observed from the video recording of the incident that the police had failed to warn the group out loud to disperse as required by section 24 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
The applicants were allegedly injured during the police intervention to disperse the group as a result of the force used by the police.
The medical report in respect of Ms Zeynep Saya stated that there were no signs of ill-treatment on her body.
The medical report in respect of Mr Hasan Ölgün stated that there were no signs of ill-treatment on his body.
The medical report in respect of Mr Müslüm Atasoy stated that there were no signs of ill-treatment on his body.
The medical report in respect of Ms Zöhre Taş stated that there were no signs of ill-treatment on her body.
The medical report in respect of Mr Nedim Çifçi stated that there were no signs of ill-treatment on his body.
The medical report in respect of Ms Hediye Kilinç stated that there were no signs of ill-treatment on her body.
The medical report in respect of Şeyho Saya indicated tenderness on the back of the right leg and on the back.
The medical report in respect of Çetin Taş indicated tenderness on the lower left side of the chest and pain while breathing.
The medical report in respect of Çetin Taş indicated tenderness and pain on the right side of the forehead.
The medical report in respect of Çetin Taş indicated a possible fracture of the ribs on the left side of the chest.
The medical report in respect of Akın Doğan indicated scratches on the back.
The medical report in respect of Ali Murat Bilgiç indicated tenderness and bruises on the left shoulder and the left arm.
The medical report in respect of Bahattin Barış Bilgiç indicated scratches on the right elbow and the right knee, and hyperaemia on the left side of the chest.

On different dates in May 1999, the applicants filed criminal complaints with the Adıyaman Public Prosecutor against those police officers who had allegedly used excessive force during the applicants' arrest on 1 May 1999.
On 17 June 1999, the Adıyaman Public Prosecutor transferred the case file to the Adıyaman Provincial Administrative Council.

The Adıyaman Public Prosecutor sought authorisation from the Adıyaman Provincial Administrative Council to bring criminal proceedings against the accused police officers, pursuant to the provisions of the Law on the Prosecution of Civil Servants.
On 16 February 2000, the Adıyaman Provincial Administrative Council found that there was not enough evidence to initiate criminal proceedings against the accused police officers.
On 16 February 2000, the Adıyaman Provincial Administrative Council refused to initiate criminal proceedings against the accused police officers.
On 1 September 2000, the applicants appealed against the decision of the Adıyaman Provincial Administrative Council of 16 February 2000.

On 14 June 2001, the Supreme Administrative Council upheld the decision of the Adıyaman Provincial Administrative Council of 16 February 2000 refusing to initiate criminal proceedings against the accused police officers.
